items.rationale: The bicycle was recovered undamaged. Sections 2.3.3 and 7.1.8(c) exclude the entire elective frame swap, not just the premium over a standard frame.
The brakes were replaced as part of routine servicing, not to repair theft damage. Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude the full line.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(a) exclude maintenance and tuning unrelated to theft damage.
Under 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10, shipping follows the excluded shop work. The invoice does not identify it as transport from the recovery site under 5.2.2(d).
Section 7.1.8(f) excludes attendance on an invoice with no covered work. The locksmith's recovery attendance is separately billed.
Under 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10, fitting charges follow the excluded upgrade and servicing they support.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.10 exclude labour of every grade on the elective upgrade and service invoice.
Under 7.1.8(a) and 7.1.10, skilled labour follows the excluded work it serves; no theft repair is established.

Section 5.2.2(a) covers necessary attendance at the recovery site even when the bicycle is undamaged. The estimated recovery total of €194 is below both the €1,000 recovery cap and the €500 aggregate mobility cap; no deductible amount is stated.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removing the lock to release the bicycle. Allow €55 per billed unit for the two-unit line, excluding any duplication of the separately billed hour under 7.1.8(g); neither cap reduces the estimate.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary lock-release labour if it is distinct from the operation charge; 7.1.8(g) bars duplicate billing. Allow €39 for one hour, consistent with Case 24, with no cap reduction.
